meta.scope: Japan batch 5 (final light densification pass) — Machinery Orders (leading investment indicator), Financial Statements Statistics of Corporations (corporate finance / profits / investment), US–Japan Trade Agreement (USJTA) as third major trade instrument, and a small number of supporting nodes. Closes remaining high-value gaps after four deeper batches so the Japan core is dense and self-contained.
meta.strategy_note: User requested one more light Japan pass. Kept deliberately compact (~8 candidates) focusing on high-citation, market-relevant or structural gaps: private capital expenditure signal, corporate sector accounts, and the bilateral US trade instrument that complements CPTPP and Japan–EU EPA.

candidates.title: Machinery Orders (機械受注統計調査)
candidates.publisher: Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI), Cabinet Office
candidates.description: Monthly survey of new orders for machinery (excluding ships and electric power) received by major manufacturers, with a quarterly outlook. Widely regarded as a leading indicator of private capital expenditure and business investment plans.
candidates.notes: Key forward-looking series for private non-residential investment in the national accounts and for market assessments of the investment cycle. Continuously cited alongside Tankan fixed-investment plans and IIP. Completes the short-term investment-signal cluster (Tankan, Machinery Orders, IIP).

candidates.title: Financial Statements Statistics of Corporations by Industry (法人企業統計調査)
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Finance — Policy Research Institute
candidates.description: Quarterly and annual sample survey of corporate financial statements providing data on sales, profits, assets, liabilities, investment in plant and equipment, inventories, and employment by industry and size of capital. Fundamental statistics used for national-accounts corporate sector estimates and for analysis of corporate profitability and balance-sheet adjustment.
candidates.notes: Core source for the non-financial corporate sector in the JSNA and for BOJ and MOF assessments of corporate financial health. Quarterly results on ordinary profits, sales, and capital expenditure are closely watched. Complements Tankan and Flow of Funds with accounting-based measures of the corporate sector.

candidates.title: United States–Japan Trade Agreement (USJTA) and United States–Japan Digital Trade Agreement
candidates.publisher: Governments of Japan and the United States
candidates.description: Bilateral trade agreement signed in 2019 that reduces or eliminates tariffs on a range of agricultural and industrial goods and includes a high-standard digital-trade chapter. Complements CPTPP and the Japan–EU EPA in Japan’s multi-track trade architecture with its largest single-country trading partner.
referenced_by: MOF Trade Statistics and BOP commentary on US partner shares and post-agreement trade flows
METI and Cabinet Office trade-policy documents
Official Japanese and US impact assessments and subsequent negotiation references
Academic and think-tank studies that treat USJTA as a baseline bilateral instrument alongside CPTPP and Japan–EU EPA
candidates.notes: Static bilateral instrument that qualifies under the expanded node definition via recurring citation in trade statistics, policy documents and impact analyses. Completes the trio of major trade agreements (CPTPP plurilateral, Japan–EU EPA bilateral with Europe, USJTA bilateral with the United States) that structure Japan’s contemporary trade-policy environment.

candidates.title: Current Survey of Production (生産動態統計調査) — reinforced notes
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
candidates.description: Monthly survey of production, shipments and inventories of manufactured goods and minerals. Primary source for the Indices of Industrial Production and a key input into national-accounts production estimates.
candidates.notes: Already conceptually covered in earlier industrial discussion; retained here with explicit node status for completeness of the METI short-term production cluster. Commodity-level detail underpins both IIP and energy/industrial policy analysis.

candidates.title: Indices of Tertiary Industry Activity — reinforced
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
candidates.description: Monthly indices of activity in the tertiary sector compiled from a range of source statistics. Complements the goods-focused IIP.
candidates.notes: Reinforced for completeness of the short-term activity triad (IIP + Tertiary + All-Industry). Widely cited for a broader reading of monthly economic momentum beyond manufacturing.

candidates.title: Trade Statistics of Japan — detailed commodity and partner matrices
candidates.description: Detailed monthly and annual customs-based trade data by HS commodity, partner country/region, customs office and mode of transport. Extends the core Trade Statistics node with the full matrix detail used for partner-share and product-level analysis.
candidates.notes: Deepens the external-sector coverage. Partner and commodity matrices are the empirical basis for assessing the effects of CPTPP, Japan–EU EPA and USJTA, and for monitoring shifts in Japan’s trade structure (e.g., semiconductor and auto exports).

candidates.title: Corporate Goods Price Index (CGPI) and Services Producer Price Index (SPPI) — reinforced producer-price cluster
candidates.description: Monthly producer price indices for goods (CGPI) and services (SPPI) traded among corporations. 2020-base. Together they provide comprehensive producer-side inflation measurement.
candidates.notes: Reinforced as a paired cluster. Essential for national-accounts deflation, margin analysis, and for understanding the transmission of global energy and intermediate-input shocks into Japanese producer prices.

candidates.title: Prefectural statistical contrast framework (Tokyo vs Okinawa / peripheral)
candidates.publisher: Various (Tokyo Metropolitan Government, Okinawa Prefecture, Cabinet Office Prefectural Accounts)
candidates.description: Conceptual and data framework that systematically compares Tokyo Metropolitan Accounts / Yearbook with peripheral prefectural yearbooks (exemplified by Okinawa) and the full set of Prefectural Accounts. Used to test hierarchy homogeneity and to surface regional heterogeneity in income, industry structure, demography and social indicators.
referenced_by: Tokyo Metropolitan Accounts and Statistical Yearbook
Cabinet Office Annual Report on Prefectural Accounts
National accounts regional analysis and fiscal equalisation studies
candidates.notes: Meta-node that makes the regional contrast explicit. Japan’s statistical system is highly decentralised at the prefectural level; the Tokyo–Okinawa (and broader core–periphery) comparison is the practical test of whether the same hierarchy of reports exists and how much independent local production occurs. Supports the homogeneity-check principle in the country strategy.
